title: Everett Robbins, pianist who died of tuberculosis
summary: Levy remembers Everett Robbins, who played at the Entertainers Cafe and died of tuberculosis.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes, a piano, when we got kind of tired playing, we stopped him at the piano and played a couple of choruses, and he liked it. And incidentally, did you hear about Everett Robbins? He played with us at the, at the Entenus Cafe. No. He died of consumption. Oh. Everett Robbins. He made one or two rags.
Oh, yes, of course, of course. I have a picture of him. Unfortunately, he isn't here, but he joined Rice up in Milwaukee.
Yes. For a time. After we left the Entenus Cafe, he went with another band, and then he caroused so much and didn't get any rest, and he drank so much that he contracted TB.
How was, he was a, he was a, very good.
